coverage.assessment: Fate/luck, the forced pace, Carter's terms, salary, taxi and blackmail joke, the photograph's uniqueness and the morning visitor all survive. Julius's account loses the link from 'saved' to 'couldn't be found, so I came over' (F1).
Exits, the taxi, the suite, lunch and the card's arrival stay clear. Dropping Carshalton Terrace, the page-boy and the restaurant choice causes no confusion. 'This morning' versus lunch is preserved.

The pinch exchange is attributed correctly. 'When did you last see your cousin?' is now unattributed (F5). Tommy's prompting question to Carter is folded into Carter's speech (F3). The shared realization about Julius is collapsed into Tommy's single turn (F6).

Carter's 'if they haven't already', 'I hope it will myself' and 'needn't be cast down if you fail' are cut (F3). Factual continuity checks all hold: Carter unnamed, three hundred each, Paris tomorrow.
Tuppence's dread stays unexplained. Inspector Brown is named only in the final line. Nothing hints at where the photograph really is or casts doubt on Julius.

The closing rhythm ('Yes, I do. No, I don't.') and Tuppence's steel image survive. Julius's idiom and energy (F2), Carter's tired hedging (F3) and Tuppence's comic deference about the Government (F4) are noticeably flattened.
The contrast between comedy and sudden menace holds, as does the theme of coincidence and luck. Cut material such as the oil/steel career and the menu is redundant.
Three dependencies are intact. For the fourth, the local endpoint survives, but partner 027 dropped the real Julius obtaining her photograph out West.

strengths: The closing sting is kept intact: Japp's card, the only-copy line, the 'unformulated dread' and Julius's halting 'Yes, I do. No, I don't. Half a second.' leading to Inspector Brown. Nothing is imported from 007.
Carter's real name stays unspoken ('Tommy murmured a name in her ear'), and 'He's IT!' is preserved.
The pinch exchange is correctly sequenced: Tuppence's steel image, the request, 'Mr. Beresford obliged', then her 'Ow! ... We've got a job!'
The blackmailer joke keeps its dark punchline, 'I'm not sure I have,' said Tuppence darkly.
Salary, return-of-post money and 'I do love money!' survive with Carter's outright laugh.
summary: The revision keeps the chapter's architecture, all eight verbatim anchors, the continuity facts and the cliffhanger ending. It does not import the next chapter's explanation. Most losses come from the revision's deeper compression of speech. Julius's account no longer says Jane vanished after rescue or that he came over to hurry the search. Carter's hedged reassurances, Tuppence's mock-deferential government complaint and much of Julius's colourful, energetic voice are thinned. Tuppence's question to Julius is also left unattributed. These are editorial repairs, not blockers.
